first_impression.reaction: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding flowers in season'. The opening line, 'Choosing wedding flowers in season starts with a date, not a mood board.', is calm and grown up, no fairytale nonsense, so I kept going. But the title says 'by month' and I was expecting a list of flowers for each month. Then I got to 'the month notes below are about the conversation rather than a fixed list' and realised it's a list of questions. Fine, and probably more honest, but I'd rather the intro had told me that upfront. We're also likely marrying overseas, so most of the Australian month detail doesn't apply to us. I skimmed it and read the imported and destination sections properly.

journey.quote: The month you marry decides which stems are at their freshest, which will need to travel, and how much room your florist has to move if a crop comes in late.
journey.reaction: That's a useful way to think about it and it's not fluffy. Feels like someone who has actually dealt with a late crop.

journey.quote: This guide follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month, with the questions worth putting to your florist for each one.
journey.reaction: I didn't really take in 'the questions' on the first skim. Because of the title I expected stems, so I felt a bit baited when I got to the month notes.

journey.section: Wedding flowers in season in Australia by month
journey.quote: What grows well in a given month varies with the region, the grower and the year, so the month notes below are about the conversation rather than a fixed list.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off and I respect it, but this is where the expectation should have been set. Arriving this far down, it reads like a caveat.

journey.quote: Ask whether the venue has water and shade for buckets during the day, and whether a bouquet can be kept chilled until the moment you leave for the ceremony.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of practical detail I'd never think to ask. Good insider stuff.

journey.quote: Waratah flowering is concentrated in spring, and growers have worked to stretch its season to reach peak demand periods such as Christmas.
journey.reaction: Nice, specific and sourced. It's the one concrete flower in the piece and I noticed it.

journey.quote: For a couple, that is the florist's and importer's work, not yours.
journey.reaction: Good. Tell me what I need to care about and skip the rest. The three questions below it are something I'd actually screenshot.

journey.quote: Agree in writing which flowers are essential to you and which the florist may substitute.
journey.reaction: Very lawyer-friendly advice. This speaks directly to my worry that something goes wrong and nobody's accountable.

journey.quote: Everything in the month by month notes above flips, or does not apply at all.
journey.reaction: For us this is the most relevant section, and the first thing it tells me is that the bit I just skimmed doesn't apply. Slightly deflating. I'd rather hear that the questions still work and I just need to use the destination's season.

journey.quote: Resist the urge to pack flowers from home.
journey.reaction: Good, clear tip. My mother would absolutely suggest this, so I'll forward this line to her.

journey.quote: The person to ask is a florist who works at the destination.
journey.reaction: Sure, but we don't know any florists in Italy or Greece. The section is fairly short for the part that actually matters to us.

journey.section: Planning your flowers and spend with your florist
journey.quote: An imported stem, a flower at the edge of its season or a date in a peak week can change a quote, and so can scale, labour and set-up.
journey.reaction: Honest about what moves the price, which I like. No numbers, but it links to a cost guide, so I'll accept that here.

journey.section: Planning your flowers and spend with your florist
journey.quote: With Wedded Concierge, you have one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, and your advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the line that actually answers 'what does end-to-end mean?'. One person, and it's in writing. That's what I want to hear.

journey.section: Plan your flowers with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, so the flowers sit within a plan that already fits your date and your destination.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is what every planner says. It's not bad, it's just more generic than the single-point-of-contact line earlier, which was the stronger one.

unanswered_questions: For a destination wedding, how do we find a florist there whose work we can trust, and does our Wedded Advisor help with that?
Even a rough idea of how much flowers usually take up in a destination wedding budget, or will the linked cost guide cover that?
Is there a real wedding we can look at where the flowers were planned around the destination's season?
would_share_with: Partner (the three questions: local, imported, backup)
Mum (the 'don't pack flowers from home' line)

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: It isn't pushy, which I appreciate. But we're 14 months out with no destination yet, and I wouldn't enquire off a flowers article alone. I'd want a couple more posts and a real wedding first. The single-point-of-contact line is what would eventually get me there.

top_3_changes: Set the 'questions, not a stem list' expectation in the intro so the title doesn't feel like bait. Old: "This guide follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month, with the questions worth putting to your florist for each one." New: "This guide follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month. What grows well shifts with region, grower and year, so rather than a fixed stem list it gives you the questions worth putting to your florist for each month."

Don't tell destination couples the month notes were wasted reading. Old: "Everything in the month by month notes above flips, or does not apply at all." New: "The questions in the month by month notes above still work; match them to the destination's season, not Australia's."

Make the closing CTA use the accountability point rather than generic reach. Old: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, so the flowers sit within a plan that already fits your date and your destination." New: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, so the flowers sit within a plan that already fits your date and your destination."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (early research, destination likely, 14 months out)
No invented brand facts; the suggested edits reuse claims already in the draft and don't add fees, commissions, supplier sourcing or vetting, or named flowers
No turn-offs invented; none of the persona's turn-offs (cliches, hard sell, vague pricing) found
HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible
